hypothesis: The recorded results of EXP-0009 through EXP-0012 are reproducible from a freshly re-downloaded 2023-2025 dataset on a different Python and numpy version. If they are not, either the dataset is not equivalent to the one the experiments ran on, or the numpy 1.26 → 2.x boundary introduces numeric drift, and in either case the validated regime filter would need re-validation.
dataset_version: nifty-5min-2023-2025 re-fetched 2026-10-13 via scripts/data_001_fetch_historical.py (DATA-001), sha256 830bd8bb6f70d1b4…, recorded in data/live_data/CHECKSUMS.json
motivation: RISK-0: the two 2023-2025 CSVs were gitignored and absent from the repository, so every experiment from EXP-0009 onward was unreproducible and unauditable. The original files were never checksummed, so a re-download could not be proven byte-identical to what the experiments ran on. This audit tests equivalence by result rather than by hash.

environment.python: 3.13.15 (recorded experiments ran on an unspecified 3.11+ interpreter)
environment.note: numpy 1.26.4 publishes no cp313 wheels, so the version boundary could not be avoided on this machine. That is what made the drift question worth answering explicitly.

method: Re-fetched the NIFTY 5-min dataset from the Upstox Analytics API over the identical date range, verified it structurally with scripts/verify_data.py (11 checks, all passed: 55,513 rows, 744 sessions, 74.6 bars/session, no duplicates, no unexplained gaps, OHLC internally consistent), then re-ran every experiment that depends on NIFTY data alone and compared each reported figure against its committed JSON record. EXP-0013 through EXP-0017 could not be included because they additionally require the India VIX daily file, which is still absent.

EXP-0009.match: EXACT — including all three regime breakdowns and their avg baseline/filtered returns (HIGH 165.4/77.0, MED 30.7/55.0, LOW 2.1/3.1)

EXP-0011.match: EXACT — including the month-by-month 2025 OOS table, e.g. 2025-01 base +128.7 / adaptive +43.2 (miss), 2025-04 +202.4 / +317.8 (beat), 2025-09 +67.4 / -2.8 (miss)

EXP-0012.match: EXACT — the simulation is seeded (np.random.default_rng(42), PCG64), and numpy guarantees stream stability for that bit generator across versions, so determinism here was expected rather than coincidental

FINDING-1.title: The re-downloaded dataset is equivalent to the original for research purposes
FINDING-1.detail: Four experiments and every sub-figure within them reproduce exactly. A dataset that differed in any material way — a missing session, a shifted timezone, a revised bar — would almost certainly perturb at least one of 36 monthly returns across 6 filter configs. It did not. This is strong evidence of equivalence despite the absence of an original checksum, and it is the best evidence obtainable now that the original files are gone.

FINDING-2.title: The numpy 1.26 → 2.5 boundary introduces no drift in this codebase
FINDING-2.detail: All four experiments reproduce bit-for-bit under numpy 2.5.4, as does EXP-0001 on its separate 2026 dataset. The concern that recorded figures might drift across the version boundary is resolved for every experiment that can currently be run. EXP-0013 through EXP-0017 remain unverified only because their VIX input is missing, not for any version reason.
FINDING-2.confidence: HIGH for the five experiments tested; UNTESTED for EXP-0013..0017

FINDING-3.title: The validated regime filter rests on sound, reproducible research
FINDING-3.detail: P70_L40d is the load-bearing component of the entire ASTRA stack. Its in-sample selection (EXP-0010), its out-of-sample walk-forward (EXP-0011), the failure of the fixed-threshold predecessor that motivated it (EXP-0009), and the Monte Carlo gate (EXP-0012) all now reproduce from scratch on a clean machine. The research core is in better standing than the documentation around it.

FINDING-4.title: EXP-0012's ruin definition is milder than the documentation claims
FINDING-4.detail: scripts/exp_0012_monte_carlo.py sets RUIN_THRESHOLD = 0.50 and labels P(ruin) as 'drawdown > 50%'. HANDOFF.md RISK-2 describes the same 17.8% figure as simulations that 'hit a 90%+ capital loss scenario'. Those are materially different events and the documented one is far more severe. RISK-2 also states that a ₹50k start reduces P(ruin); the simulation reports identical percentile returns for ₹20k, ₹50k, ₹1L and ₹5L starts, because it models percentage returns and is therefore scale-invariant. The model gives no support for a start-size effect on ruin probability — and omits the real constraint that penalises small accounts, namely lot indivisibility.
FINDING-4.confidence: HIGH — read directly from the script and confirmed against its output

conclusion: HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED. All four NIFTY-only experiments reproduce exactly from a freshly re-downloaded dataset on Python 3.13 / numpy 2.5.4, including every regime breakdown, all six filter configs, the month-by-month out-of-sample table, and the full Monte Carlo percentile distribution. RISK-0 is resolved for the NIFTY dataset: the validated regime filter is now reproducible and auditable from a clean clone, and the dataset is checksummed so this cannot silently regress. Two caveats remain. EXP-0013 through EXP-0017 — the VIX-dependent half of the stack, which includes the entire compounding and position-sizing line of research — are still unreproducible pending the India VIX daily file. And reproducibility is not validity: these experiments reproduce their own recorded numbers, which says nothing about the open questions in DECISION-008 and DECISION-010, nor about the EXP-0016 results conflict.
caveats: CAVEAT-1: Equivalence is inferred from identical results, not proven by hash. The original files were never checksummed, so byte-identity is unprovable in principle.
CAVEAT-2: This audit re-ran experiments; it did not re-audit their methodology. Leakage, look-ahead and multiple-testing questions are unchanged by a reproduction.

CAVEAT-3: EXP-0010 remains an in-sample selection over 6 configs. Its own record flags this; EXP-0011's walk-forward is what addresses it. Reproducing both does not reduce the multiple-testing exposure.

CAVEAT-4: The NIFTY file was re-fetched from Upstox, whereas HANDOFF.md section 7 lists NSE as the source for both files. Upstox is the source the committed fetcher uses, and the results confirm it is the right one.
